notes: Regional Chair K. Redman called the meeting to order at 9:01 a.m.

items.title: Martha Bricker, Wilmot
notes: M. Bricker spoke to Council regarding well interference, and shared concerns related to the composition of the proposed Well Interference Committee. M. Bricker asked the Committee to include independent members of the public on the Committee.

items.title: EES-WIM-26-015, Mannheim Service Area Water Capacity Constraint - Update on Work Underway - August 2026
notes:
Ken Brothers, Commissioner of Water and Wastewater, introduced the report and gave an overview of the work underway. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda.

K. Brothers stated that Water Allocation Policy Agreements were executed for Cambridge, Kitchener, Waterloo, and Woolwich, with Wilmot to consider the Agreement at the upcoming August Council Meeting. K. Brothers further stated that the first assignment of water has been provided, and Area Municipalities are now allocating waster based on local policies.

K. Brothers provided an update on infrastructure, explaining the work underway at the Mannheim Side Stream Project, Greenbrook, the Maple Grove Water System, and the Grand Water System.

Rod Regier, Commissioner of Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, provided an update regarding growth and development, stating that work on data sharing and processing requests for Transfers of Serving Commitment is underway. R. Reiger noted that no requests have been made to the Region for a Forward Looking Servicing Agreement to date.

Connie MacDonalds, Commissioner of Resident Experience, provided a communications update, noting ongoing plans including progress updates, continued website and social updates, highlighting infrastructure solutions, and well interference engagement.

K. Brothers concluded with next steps, which include finalized site prep for the Mannheim Side Stream Project, a progress update scheduled for August 13, 2026, reports on infrastructure updates, resources, and well interference planned to come forward in September, and a workshop with OCWA in August. K. Brothers stated that a report will come back to Council in October regarding the OCWA workshop.

items.title: EES-WIM-26-016, Draft Policy and Procedures for Groundwater Interference Complaints in the Region of Waterloo
notes:
K. Brothers introduced the report and gave an overview of the draft Policy and Procedures for Groundwater Interference Complaints. A copy of the report is attached to the agenda.

Amy Shaw, Director of Water and Wastewater, provided an overview of the policy review and recommendation process, which included a background review, a jurisdictional scan, stakeholder engagement, and technical and regulatory alignment. A. Shaw elaborated on the engagement process, which included six (6) sessions between June and August, two (2) public information sessions, and an online and in-print feedback survey.

A. Shaw explained the themes identified in the engagement process, which included support for transparency, an independent appeals process, clearer communication and greater involvement, timely response and emergency water supply, remedies that fully restore water supply, science-based and independent decisions, increased awareness and accessibility of the complaint process, and trust and accountability.

A. Shaw explained the process for well interference complaints under the new policy, the composition of the committee, and the appeal process. A. Shaw stated that next steps include an additional in-person public information session in August, and a finalized Well Interference Complaint Policy and a Draft Terms of Reference for the Committee to be brought back to Council on September 9, 2026.

In response to Council, A. Shaw stated that the composition of the Well Interference Appeal Committee is aligned with comparable municipalities and historical committees in the Region. A. Shaw confirmed that staff can come back with more options for selecting committee composition in September.

Responding to Council, A. Shaw stated that the decision to not recommended an appointed community member on the Well Interference Appeal Committee was to ensure independence and protect the privacy of complainants.

A. Shaw confirmed that the term resident used throughout the report can be changed to reflect residential, commercial, and agricultural applicants.

Council discussed options related to committee composition, including the possibility to include elected officials from other jurisdictions, technical experts, and community members.

A. Shaw noted that an independent consultant and a well technician will be involved in the evaluation of complaints, provide their written recommendations and will attend appeal hearings as technical experts. A. Shaw emphasized that these individuals, while being paid by the Region, will be bound by the professional obligations of their licensing. She stated that this ensures an independent process.

In response to Council, A. Shaw explained that proactive monitoring is done in the Region of Waterloo to prevent well interferences, and we do more than we are obligated to do in our permit to take water. A. Shaw clarified that staff would be open to further testing.

In response to Council, Matt Alexander, Manager of Hydrogeology at AECOM, stated that the Guelph Well Interference Committee does not include any community members.

In response to Council, A. Shaw confirmed that the recharge time for the Mannheim Aquifer differs between locations. Karl Belan, Acting Manager of Hydrogeology and Water Programs, further explained that the effects of water taking is generally seen much more quickly than recharge occurs.

In response to Council, A. Shaw explained that trigger levels are actively being monitored to prevent well interference, and that trigger levels can be modified if needed. 

Responding to Council, A. Shaw confirmed that contracts for a consultant and well technician will follow the Region's purchasing by-law. Wayne Steffler, Commissioner of Corporate Services, added that the purchasing by-law includes measures to prevent conflicts of interest.

Responding to a question from Council concerning the cost of removing the cap on compensation amounts, A. Shaw explained that an initial assessment will be done to ensure only cases in which the Region could reasonably be responsible for a well interference will move forward to the next stage of investigation. A. Shaw further explained that remedies would depend on the recommendations and the specific incident if the Region's pumping was found to be the cause.
